angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 227,703 km at 47.32 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.1308 +/- 0.0179 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 47.32 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3273 +/- 0.0029 solar radii from Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2015 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.281B/abstract): 227,703 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.3041 +/- 0.0353 solar masses from Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2015 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.281B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3297 +/- 14 K from Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2015 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.281B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barkaoui et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2015 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.281B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2015.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.891, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
